'''Akagi Shrine''' (赤城神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|ja|神道|12=draft}} shrine located in {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=draft}}) and is also regarded as a potential site of the Second Shrine of {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国|12=draft}}. It was formerly designated as a Prefectural Shrine under the pre-World War II Modern Shrine Ranking System. It is officially called "Akagi Shrine," but to distinguish it from other shrines of the same name, it is also referred to as "'''Miyosawa Akagi Shrine'''" (三夜沢赤城神社). Among the approximately 300 Akagi shrines across the country, especially centered around the Kantō region, this shrine is considered one of the most likely to be the original main shrine. == Overview == The shrine sits on the southern mountainside of {{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft}} in central Gunma Prefecture. Prior to the Meiji period, the shrine consisted of two separate shrines (East and West), but they were unified into a single entity during the Meiji era. The approach to the shrine diverges into three directions at the first torii gate: toward {{ill|Ōgo|ja|大胡町|12=draft}} in the south, Naegashima in the east, and Ichinoseki in the west. The path toward Ōgo retains a row of pine trees planted during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}. The honden (main sanctuary) and nakamon (middle gate) are designated as Important Cultural Properties by Gunma Prefecture. Approximately 500 meters south of the honden along the path is the sōmon (main gate), which is also a prefectural cultural property. Between the haiden (worship hall) and nakamon stands the "Tawara Sugi," a cedar tree designated as a Natural Monument by the prefecture. Additionally, the grounds include the "Monument of Jindai Moji," established in March 1870, a relic of {{ill|Fukko Shintō|ja|復古神道|12=draft}}, and designated as an Important Cultural Property by Maebashi City. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft}}}} * Akagi-no-Kami * {{ill|Toyoki-Irihiko-no-Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}} == History == === Establishment === The shrine's establishment date is unknown. According to shrine tradition, it was founded when Toyoki-Irihiko-no-Mikoto began ruling over {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上毛野国|12=draft}}, accompanied by Ōkuninushi. About 1.3 km up from the shrine lies a ritual site centered around a large rock known as {{ill|Hitsuishi|ja|櫃石|12=draft}}, which indicates the presence of ancient Shinto practices. === General History ===
Transition of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine

=== Heian Period === According to the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft}}, in 839 (Jōwa 6), the shrine received the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}} records that the shrine was promoted multiple times between 867 (Jōgan 9) and 880 (Gangyō 4), eventually reaching Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade. It is said that by around 1028 (Chōgen 9), it was promoted to Senior First Rank. {{Shrine | name = Akagi Shrine | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|ja|神道|12=draft}} | image = {{ill|Akagi Shrine (Miyosawa) Front View|ja|赤城神社 (Miyosawa) shoumen|12=draft}}

Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} | establishment = Unknown | main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} | alternate_name = Miyosawa Akagi Shrine | talisman_place = | festival = {{ill|May 5|ja|5月5日|12=draft}} | sacred_event = | map = {{Location map|Japan Gunma#Japan|label=Akagi Shrine|lat_deg=36|lat_min=29|lat_sec=02.6|lon_deg=139|lon_min=10|lon_sec=39.7|mark={{ill|Shinto Torii|ja|神社鳥居|12=draft}} icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=10|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|29|3.94|N|139|10|41.08|E}}}} }} {{GeoGroup}} [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Grand Torii}}]] '''Akagi Shrine''' (赤城神社) is a {{ill|shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in Miyosawa-cho, {{ill|Maebashi City|ja|前橋市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meishin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=draft}}) {{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社|12=draft}}, as well as a Nomiya Ronsha of {{ill|Ueno Province|ja|上野国|12=draft}}, and formerly a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}}. Although its official name is "Akagi Shrine", to distinguish it from other Akagi Shrines it is also called "'''Miyosawa Akagi Shrine''' (みよさわあかぎじんじゃ)". It is one of the principal shrines, presumed to be the main shrine among approximately 300 Akagi Shrines across the country, mainly in the {{ill|Kanto region|ja|関東地方|12=draft}}. == Overview == Located on the southern hillside of {{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft}} in central {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}, the shrine was once regarded as having two shrines (East and West) before the Meiji era, but later became a single shrine. The approach splits into three directions: one with the first torii leading south toward the {{ill|Grand Torii|ja|大鳥居|12=draft}} and the Ōogomachi area, one east toward Naegashima, and one west toward Ichinoseki. The road continuing in the Ōogomachi direction still retains a pine avenue planted during the Edo period. Both the main hall and the middle gate are designated as important cultural properties by the prefecture. Along the approach, about 500 meters south of the main hall, stands the Soumon (main gate), also designated as an important cultural property. Additionally, between the worship hall and the middle gate, immediately in front of the middle gate, is the "Tawara Cedar", a natural monument designated by Gunma Prefecture. The shrine grounds also include a "Jindai Moji Stele" erected in March 1870 (Meiji 3), regarded as an artifact of the restoration of ancient Shinto, and designated as an important cultural property by the city. == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft}}}} * {{ill|Akagi God|ja|赤城神|12=draft}} (Akagi no Kami) * {{ill|Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft}} (Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}} (Ōkuninushi-no-mikoto) == History == [[File:MountAkagi.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|{{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft}} (Sacred Object)}}]] === Establishment === The establishment date is unknown. According to the shrine’s tradition, in ancient times when {{ill|Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft}} came to rule {{ill|Kozuke Province|ja|上毛野国|12=draft}}, he enshrined {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}}. About 1.3 km uphill from the shrine, a ritual site centered on a stone called the "Hitsuishi" remains, suggesting ancient worship practices. === Chronological Overview ===
Chronological Transition of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine

(Worshiped deities: {{ill|Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft}} and {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴神|12=draft}})}} {{familytree/end}}
==== Heian Period ==== In the ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft}}'', it is recorded that in the 6th year of the {{ill|Shōwa|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (839) the deity was conferred the rank of Junior Fifth Rank Lower; in the ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}}'' it is recorded that between the 9th and 16th years of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (867–874) the deity was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank Upper to Senior Fifth Rank Lower, and in the 4th year of the {{ill|Genkei|ja|元慶|12=draft}} era (880) to Senior Fourth Rank Upper.A record in the Nagagen period document ''Ueno Province Alternating Records'' lists the rank as Senior First, though no promotion record exists. Later, in the medieval period, the shrine became the Second Shrine of {{ill|Ueno Province|ja|上野国|12=draft}}. However, debate exists as to whether the deity mentioned in these records—with a Ronsha present at another shrine—refers to Miyosawa Akagi Shrine (see {{ill|Akagi Shrine#History|ja|赤城神社#歴史|12=draft}}). In the 14th century collection of legends ''{{ill|Shinto Shu|ja|神道集|12=draft}}'', the small pond of Mount Akagi’s crater lake, the large pond, and the central crater’s Jizodake are deified. The small pond god is associated with {{ill|Kokūzō Bosatsu|ja|虚空蔵菩薩|12=draft}}, the large pond god with {{ill|Senju Kannon|ja|千手観音|12=draft}}, and Jizodake is identified with {{ill|Jizō Bosatsu|ja|地蔵菩薩|12=draft}} (the latter being a later addition). According to records handed down in the West Shrine, the West Shrine enshrined Kokūzō and Senju Kannon, while the East Shrine enshrined Jizō. According to the "Miyagi Murashi", the Miyosawa Akagi Shrine is distinct from the government shrine Akagi seen in texts such as the ''Rokukokushi''. Originally, the East Shrine was established around the late 13th to early 14th century as "Akagi Shrine" along with the flourishing of the Jizodake faith; subsequently, the shrine located in the area known as "Former Miyosawa"The Miyosawa Akagi Shrine tradition states that the shrine grounds were relocated, with the eastern site known as Former Miyosawa. The Utsū Ruins discovered there have been identified as the former shrine site. relocated next to the East Shrine. This new site became the West Shrine, estimated to have been established around the 1st year of the {{ill|Jōwa|ja|貞和|12=draft}} era (circa 1345). The former Miyosawa shrine is also said to have been the mountain shrine of the Nomiya Akagi Shrine. After the West Shrine was relocated, Miyosawa Akagi Shrine came to consist of both an East and a West Shrine, although the longstanding East Shrine was stronger. During the Sengoku period, documents indicate that almost all references to the shrine included "Miyosawa" in the name, not recognizing it as the main shrine of Akagi. However, by the 4th year of the {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|12=draft}} era (1576), after the Nomiya Akagi Shrine in Ninomiya Town was destroyed by local rivals, there were no shrines rivaling the Miyosawa Akagi Shrine and its East Shrine, and it came to be recognized as the main shrine of Akagi.According to the "Miyagi Murashi". ==== Edo Period ==== On February 20 in the 17th year of the {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} era (1612), a donation from residents of Ōmaeda Village (present-day Ōmaeda-cho, Maebashi City) resulted in a row of pine trees being planted along the approach. In the 12th year of the {{ill|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|12=draft}} era (1762), the East Shrine was conferred Senior First Rank, followed by the West Shrine in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiwa|ja|明和|12=draft}} era (1765). In the 12th year of the {{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政|12=draft}} era (1800), the {{ill|Daidō Akagi Shrine|ja|大洞赤城神社|12=draft}} of Maebashi’s Fujimicho, Akagi Mountain, using the title "Main Shrine", initiated litigation against Miyosawa Akagi Shrine’s attendant temple, Jujōji. In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|12=draft}} era (1802), the Miyosawa side appealed to the shogunate’s Temple and Shrine Magistrate, but the matter was resolved by returning it to state jurisdiction. The litigation was prolonged, and an agreement regarding the use of names was reached in the {{ill|Bunka|ja|文久|12=draft}} 13th year (1816). ==== From the Meiji Period Onwards ==== In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} era (1869), due to the policy of abolishing Buddhism, two shrine-temples—Ryūseki-ji of the East Shrine and Shinkō-ji of the West Shrine—were closed. Thereafter, the two shrines of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine, formerly East and West, merged into a single shrine. Although documents from the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|12=draft}} era (1802) already treated it as a single shrine, it was officially designated as such in the early Meiji period. However, as the shrine’s records do not mention the merger, the exact timing remains unknown. No buildings were erected at the former West Shrine site, and at the East Shrine site the current shrine buildings (the main hall and the middle gate) were constructed. A record exists of a topping-out ceremony held on November 25 (old calendar) in Meiji 2 (1869). In 1894 (Meiji 27), the worship hall burned down and was later rebuilt. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it was initially a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, later elevated to a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}}. In 1935 (Shōwa 10), a movement for elevation to a {{ill|Kokuhēisha|ja|国幣社|12=draft}} arose, and in 1944 (Shōwa 19) a provisional decision for {{ill|Kokuhēichūsha|ja|国幣中社|12=draft}} was issued; however, during the process the end of the war and directives from the GHQ led to the abolition of the shrine ranking system, leaving it as a Prefectural Shrine. === Shrine Ranks === * Records in the ''{{ill|Rokukokushi|ja|六国史|12=draft}}'' record the conferral of shrine ranks for "Akagi God" (though interpretations vary beyond this shrine): ** In the 6th year of the {{ill|Shōwa|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (839), in June, he was conferred Junior Fifth Rank Lower (''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft}}'') ** In the 9th year of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (867), on June 20, he was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank Upper to Senior Fifth Rank Lower (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}}'') ** On December 25 of the 11th year of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観|12=draft}} era (869), he was conferred Senior Fifth Rank Upper (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') ** On March 14 of the 16th year of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観|12=draft}} era (874), he was conferred Junior Fourth Rank Lower (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') ** On May 25 of the 4th year of the {{ill|Genkei|ja|元慶|12=draft}} era (880), he was conferred Junior Fourth Rank Upper – with the inscription reading either "Akagi Ishi-no-Kami" or "Akagi Numano-Kami"Manuscript variations exist between "Akagi Ishi-no-Kami" and "Akagi Numano-Kami". * After the Rokukokushi period: ** Around the 3rd year of the {{ill|Chōgen|ja|長元|12=draft}} era (circa 1030), he was conferred Senior First Rank (as per the ''Ueno Province Alternating Records'') ** Senior First Rank (as per the ''Ueno Province Shrine Name Records'') – recorded as "Akagi Daimyōjin" * 18th Century: ** In the 12th year of the {{ill|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|12=draft}} era (1762), the East Shrine received Senior First Rank ** In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiwa|ja|明和|12=draft}} era (1765), the West Shrine received Senior First Rank == Shrine Facilities == === Shrine Buildings === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall (Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} style with three bays on the front and two on the sides, in a gabled roof design with copper plate roofing. The chigi (roof finials) are internally tapered, with eight support beams (katsugi) installed. It is said, along with the middle gate, to have been built in 1869 (Meiji 2){{Cite web|title=III Akagi Mountain Faith and Historical Scenery of the Southern Foot Settlements|url=https://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/material/files/group/59/rekimachi_2shou_3.pdf|website=Maebashi City|accessdate=2025-02-04}}. Its construction reflects the influences of the then prevalent Shinto-Buddhism separation and restoration of ancient Shinto, and together with the middle gate it is designated as a tangible cultural property of Gunma Prefecture[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01034&insgpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Main Hall and Middle Gate] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). Within the main hall is an inner palace enshrined as the divine seat (kamiza). An inscription behind the door states "Gifted by Minenari Shige Yorin", and it is attributed to the offering by the lord of {{ill|Nintenkimazono Castle|ja|新田金山城|12=draft}}, Minenari Shige Yorin. Constructed in a wooden hōkei style (not “square-style”) with a plank roof and a height of 117 cm, featuring chimaki-adorned pillars and lattice doors reminiscent of Zen style, it is characteristic of the Muromachi period and designated as a tangible cultural property of Gunma Prefecture[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01033&insgpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Inner Palace] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). The middle gate, a four-legged gate standing in front of the main hall, is a gabled roof structure with copper roofing, also said to have been built in 1869 (Meiji 2). The inner palace within the main hall, as well as the main hall and middle gate, were designated as important cultural properties of Gunma Prefecture in 1963 (Showa 38) and 1973 (Showa 48) respectively. File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) haiden.JPG|Worship Hall File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) nakamon.JPG|Middle Gate (Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) kaguraden.JPG|Kagura Hall === Around the Shrine Buildings === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) tawara-sugi.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Tawara Cedar (Gunma Prefecture-designated Natural Monument)}}{{small|Middle Gate is at lower left.}}]] The "Tawara Cedar" refers to three large cedar trees standing immediately to the south of the middle gate and its western neighbor. The two trees in front of the main hall stand side by side. According to legend, they were planted as offerings by {{ill|Fujiwara no Hidesato|ja|藤原秀郷|12=draft}} (also known as Tawara Tōta) during his journey to the Ueno government office to subdue {{ill|Taira no Masakado|ja|平将門|12=draft}}. They have been designated as a natural monument by Gunma Prefecture[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01037&insgpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Tawara Cedar] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). A similar legend is recounted for the cedar at {{ill|Ichinomiya Nukemae Shrine|ja|一之宮貫前神社|12=draft}}, suggesting the aspirations of medieval warriors towards honorOn-site explanatory board.. Many other large cedar trees also stand within the shrine grounds. Also present is the "Jindai Moji Stele", an inscribed stone believed to bear characters from before the introduction of Chinese script, erected in March of Meiji 3 as an artifact of ancient Shinto. The inscription was written by the adopted son of {{ill|Hirata Atsutane|ja|平田鐵胤|12=draft}}, with the divine text composed by his son, En'in. The divine text "Manahitokoronarukowe yoshi" is written in the style of the Abiru script passed down within the Abiru family of Tsushima. Additionally, about 200 m east of the shrine grounds along the road to the Hitsuishi, there is a beech tree designated as a natural monument by the city, and a treasure pagoda (Akagi Tower) designated as a city-important cultural property. File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) shindaimojihi.JPG|Jindai Moji Stele (City-designated Important Cultural Property) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) buna.JPG|Miyosawa Beech (City-designated Natural Monument) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) keidaisandou.JPG|Approach Path in the Shrine Grounds File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) ike.JPG|Sacred Pond === Within Mount Akagi === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) hituishi.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Hitsuishi (Gunma Prefecture-designated Historic Site)}}]] A ritual site centered on a massive stone known as "Hitsuishi" is located about 1.3 km up Mount Akagi from the shrine grounds ({{Coord|36|29|38.43|N|139|10|30.42|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=Hitsuishi}}). It measures approximately 4.7 m in length, 2.7 m in width, 2.8 m in height, with a circumference of 12.2 m. Numerous ritual objects have been found in the vicinity, and it was designated as a historic site by Gunma Prefecture in 1963 (Showa 38)[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.178167933333,36.4909051337386&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01036&insgpos=139.178167933333,36.4909051337386&accept=939820130608102329 Hitsuishi] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System).[http://www.gunmaibun.org/cgi-bin/iseki/database.cgi?cmd=dp&num=23369&dp= Hitsuishi] (Gunma Prefecture Buried Cultural Property Survey Group). === Approach (Sandō) === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) soumon.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Soumon (Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Property)}}]] The approach from the Soumon to National Route 353 is lined with numerous pine trees, preserved as an Edo-period pine avenue. According to the "Akagi Shrine Chronicle", in the 17th year of the {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} era (1612) approximately 1,200 pine trees were planted along the approach by donation from Hikobe of Ōmaeda Village (present-day Ōmaeda-cho, Maebashi City), each estimated to be around 400 years old. In addition, about 30,000 rhododendron plants were also planted, making the area famous in spring[http://akagi-yama.jp/archives/330 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Pine Avenue and Rhododendron Group] (Akagi Mountain Portal Site). The Soumon is a Takamado-mon built during the Edo period (exact date unknown). It is located about 450 m south of the shrine grounds ({{Coord|36|28|49.61|N|139|10|39.36|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=Soumon}}). Although the "Akagi Shrine Chronicle" records its construction in the 1st year of the {{ill|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|12=draft}} era (1751), some older materials are also evident. As few Takamado-mon from the early modern period exist in Gunma Prefecture, it was designated as a tangible cultural property in 1978 (Showa 53)[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333%2C36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500%2C500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000010&insgpos=139.181267133333%2C36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329&Map.x=246&Map.y=352 Akagi Shrine Soumon] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) ishidono.JPG|Ishidono (City-designated Important Cultural Property) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) sandou.JPG|Approach Path File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii ({{Coord|36|28|36.74|N|139|10|43.16|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}) == Festivals == * Shihō Haijinja and New Year Festival ({{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|12=draft}})The festival events are recorded in the shrine’s tradition. * Shūsei-e ({{ill|January 5|ja|1月5日|12=draft}}) * Tsutsugayu Sacred Event ({{ill|January 15|ja|1月15日|12=draft}}) * Nenki Festival ({{ill|February 19|ja|2月19日|12=draft}}) * Gochin Festival (afternoon in March) * Sacred Procession (early April) – A mikoshi parade from Nomiya Akagi Shrine to Miyosawa. * Annual Festival ({{ill|May 5|ja|5月5日|12=draft}}) * Gochin Festival (afternoon in November) * Sacred Procession (early December) – A mikoshi parade from Nomiya Akagi Shrine to Miyosawa. * New Rice Thanksgiving Festival (Shinjō-sai) ({{ill|December 10|ja|12月10日|12=draft}}) == Cultural Properties == === Important Artifacts (National Designation) === * Jadeite magatama (excavated near the Akagi Shrine Hitsuishi) – Designated on July 13, 1939 (Showa 14)'Catalog of Important Artifacts' (Shibunkaku, 1972), Volume 1, p.30The Maebashi City official website gives the designation date as "July 30, Showa 14", but the official gazette date is July 13 of the same year. === Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Inner Palace of the Main Hall – Designated on September 4, 1963 (Showa 38). ** Main Hall and Middle Gate – Designated on April 25, 1973 (Showa 48). ** Ancient Documents – 45 documents from Eiroku 3 (1560) to Keichō 18 (1613). Designated on April 25, Showa 48. ** Soumon – Designated on August 25, Showa 53. * Historic Sites ** Hitsuishi – Designated on September 4, 1963 (Showa 38), with an additional designation on June 25, 1985 (Showa 60). * Natural Monuments ** The Tawara Cedar of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine – Designated on April 25, 1973 (Showa 48). === Maebashi City-designated Cultural Properties === * Important Cultural Properties (Tangible) ** Jindai Moji Stele in the shrine grounds – Designated on April 1, 1978 (Showa 53). ** Treasure Pagoda (Akagi Tower) – Designated on April 1, 1978 (Showa 53). * Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties ** Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Taida Kagura – 13 troupes are offered on January 1, January 5, and May 5. Designated on July 4, Showa 60. * Natural Monuments ** The Beech of Miyosawa – Designated on April 1, 1980 (Showa 55). == Related Locations == * Former Miyosawa (Murozawa, Kasukawa-cho, Maebashi City) : Considered to be the old shrine site of the West Shrine prior to its relocation. Foundation stones, presumed to date from the Heian period, have been discovered'Place Names of Gunma Prefecture' – Murozawa Section, Kasukawa Village, Setagaya District. * Utsū Ruins ({{ill|Utsū Ruins|ja|宇通遺跡|12=draft}}) (Nakanosawa, Kasukawa-cho, Maebashi City, {{ウィキ座標|36|29|20.11|N|139|12|02.23|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=Utsū Ruins}}) : Ruins located in a forest in the upper reaches of the Kasukawa River. Discovered during a forest fire in 1965 (Showa 40), investigations were partial but identified foundation stone structures suggesting the remains of a temple from the syncretic period. It is speculated to be the former location of Akagi Shrine, and its relation to the multi-storied pagoda on the mountain (in {{ill|Kiryū City|ja|桐生市|12=draft}}, built in the 20th year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft}} (801)) has been noted'Place Names of Gunma Prefecture' – Utsū Ruins Section, Kasukawa Village, Setagaya District.[http://www.gunmaibun.org/cgi-bin/iseki/database.cgi?cmd=dp&num=22585&dp= Utsū Ruins] (Gunma Prefecture Buried Cultural Property Survey Group). == Local Information == '''Location''' * {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}{{ill|Maebashi City|ja|前橋市|12=draft}} Miyosawa-cho, 114 '''Access''' * From {{ill|Jōmō Electric Railway|ja|上毛電気鉄道|12=draft}}{{ill|Jōmō Line|ja|上毛電気鉄道上毛線|12=draft}} {{ill|Ōogoe Station|ja|大胡駅|12=draft}}, take the [http://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/kurashi/143/168/166/p001744.html {{ill|Maebashi City Furusato Bus|ja|前橋市ふるさとバス|12=draft}}] (demand bus) and alight at the "Akagi Shrine" bus stop (a short walk from there). '''Surroundings''' * {{ill|Akagi South-Facing Senbonzakura|ja|赤城南面千本桜|12=draft}} – A cherry tree avenue extending approximately 3.5 km. == References == '''Notes''' {{Reflist|group="note"}} '''Sources''' {{Reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * "Akagi Shrine Yuiosho-ryakuki" (Shrine Tradition Record) * Miyagi Murashi Editorial Committee, ed. "Miyagi Murashi" (Miyagi Village, 1973) * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Place Names of Gunma Prefecture" (Heibonsha) – Section on Akagi Shrine in Setagaya District, Miyagi Village * Kajima Katsuo, "Akagi Shrine" in {{ill|Kenichi Tanikawa|ja|谷川健一|12=draft}} ed., ''Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Sites – 11 Kanto'' (Hakusuisha) == See Also == {{Commonscat|Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa)|赤城神社}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|12=draft}} ** {{ill|Akagi Shrine (Maebashi City Fujimicho, Mount Akagi)|ja|赤城神社 (前橋市富士見町赤城山)|12=draft}} ** {{ill|Nomiya Akagi Shrine|ja|二宮赤城神社|12=draft}} == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/250201.html {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|12=draft}}] – Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program “Compilation of Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials” {{神道 横}} {{citation needed|あかきしんしやまえはししみよさわまち}} {{draft categories| [[Category:History of Maebashi City]] [[Category:Architecture of Maebashi City]] [[Category:Meishin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha of Ueno Province]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrines in Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Akagi Shrines]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] }} [[ja:赤城神社 (前橋市三夜沢町)]] [[sn:Miyosawa Akagi Shrine]] [[ja:赤城神社]]

revision.text:
'''Akagi Shrine''' (赤城神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|ja|神道|12=draft}} shrine located in {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=draft}}) and is also regarded as a potential site of the Second Shrine of {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国|12=draft}}. It was formerly designated as a Prefectural Shrine under the pre-World War II Modern Shrine Ranking System. It is officially called "Akagi Shrine," but to distinguish it from other shrines of the same name, it is also referred to as "'''Miyosawa Akagi Shrine'''" (三夜沢赤城神社). Among the approximately 300 Akagi shrines across the country, especially centered around the Kantō region, this shrine is considered one of the most likely to be the original main shrine. == Overview == The shrine sits on the southern mountainside of {{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft}} in central Gunma Prefecture. Prior to the Meiji period, the shrine consisted of two separate shrines (East and West), but they were unified into a single entity during the Meiji era. The approach to the shrine diverges into three directions at the first torii gate: toward {{ill|Ōgo|ja|大胡町|12=draft}} in the south, Naegashima in the east, and Ichinoseki in the west. The path toward Ōgo retains a row of pine trees planted during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}}. The honden (main sanctuary) and nakamon (middle gate) are designated as Important Cultural Properties by Gunma Prefecture. Approximately 500 meters south of the honden along the path is the sōmon (main gate), which is also a prefectural cultural property. Between the haiden (worship hall) and nakamon stands the "Tawara Sugi," a cedar tree designated as a Natural Monument by the prefecture. Additionally, the grounds include the "Monument of Jindai Moji," established in March 1870, a relic of {{ill|Fukko Shintō|ja|復古神道|12=draft}}, and designated as an Important Cultural Property by Maebashi City. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft}}}} * Akagi-no-Kami * {{ill|Toyoki-Irihiko-no-Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}} == History == === Establishment === The shrine's establishment date is unknown. According to shrine tradition, it was founded when Toyoki-Irihiko-no-Mikoto began ruling over {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上毛野国|12=draft}}, accompanied by Ōkuninushi. About 1.3 km up from the shrine lies a ritual site centered around a large rock known as {{ill|Hitsuishi|ja|櫃石|12=draft}}, which indicates the presence of ancient Shinto practices. === General History ===
Transition of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine
{{familytree/start|style=font-size:90%}} ... (family tree preserved as in source) {{familytree/end}}
=== Heian Period === According to the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft}}, in 839 (Jōwa 6), the shrine received the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}} records that the shrine was promoted multiple times between 867 (Jōgan 9) and 880 (Gangyō 4), eventually reaching Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade. It is said that by around 1028 (Chōgen 9), it was promoted to Senior First Rank. {{Shrine | name = Akagi Shrine | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|ja|神道|12=draft}} | image = {{ill|Akagi Shrine (Miyosawa) Front View|ja|赤城神社 (Miyosawa) shoumen|12=draft}}

Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}} | establishment = Unknown | main_hall = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} | alternate_name = Miyosawa Akagi Shrine | talisman_place = | festival = {{ill|May 5|ja|5月5日|12=draft}} | sacred_event = | map = {{Location map|Japan Gunma#Japan|label=Akagi Shrine|lat_deg=36|lat_min=29|lat_sec=02.6|lon_deg=139|lon_min=10|lon_sec=39.7|mark={{ill|Shinto Torii|ja|神社鳥居|12=draft}} icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20|float=center|border=none|position=top|width=200|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|marker=religious-shinto|zoom=10|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|coord={{coord|36|29|3.94|N|139|10|41.08|E}}}} }} {{GeoGroup}} [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Grand Torii}}]] '''Akagi Shrine''' (赤城神社) is a {{ill|shrine|ja|神社|12=draft}} located in Miyosawa-cho, {{ill|Maebashi City|ja|前橋市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meishin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=draft}}) {{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社|12=draft}}, as well as a Nomiya Ronsha of {{ill|Ueno Province|ja|上野国|12=draft}}, and formerly a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}}. Although its official name is "Akagi Shrine", to distinguish it from other Akagi Shrines it is also called "'''Miyosawa Akagi Shrine''' (みよさわあかぎじんじゃ)". It is one of the principal shrines, presumed to be the main shrine among approximately 300 Akagi Shrines across the country, mainly in the {{ill|Kanto region|ja|関東地方|12=draft}}. == Overview == Located on the southern hillside of {{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft}} in central {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}, the shrine was once regarded as having two shrines (East and West) before the Meiji era, but later became a single shrine. The approach splits into three directions: one with the first torii leading south toward the {{ill|Grand Torii|ja|大鳥居|12=draft}} and the Ōogomachi area, one east toward Naegashima, and one west toward Ichinoseki. The road continuing in the Ōogomachi direction still retains a pine avenue planted during the Edo period. Both the main hall and the middle gate are designated as important cultural properties by the prefecture. Along the approach, about 500 meters south of the main hall, stands the Soumon (main gate), also designated as an important cultural property. Additionally, between the worship hall and the middle gate, immediately in front of the middle gate, is the "Tawara Cedar", a natural monument designated by Gunma Prefecture. The shrine grounds also include a "Jindai Moji Stele" erected in March 1870 (Meiji 3), regarded as an artifact of the restoration of ancient Shinto, and designated as an important cultural property by the city. == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft}}}} * {{ill|Akagi God|ja|赤城神|12=draft}} (Akagi no Kami) * {{ill|Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft}} (Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}} (Ōkuninushi-no-mikoto) == History == [[File:MountAkagi.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|{{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft}} (Sacred Object)}}]] === Establishment === The establishment date is unknown. According to the shrine’s tradition, in ancient times when {{ill|Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft}} came to rule {{ill|Kozuke Province|ja|上毛野国|12=draft}}, he enshrined {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft}}. About 1.3 km uphill from the shrine, a ritual site centered on a stone called the "Hitsuishi" remains, suggesting ancient worship practices. === Chronological Overview ===
Chronological Transition of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine

==== Heian Period ==== In the ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft}}'', it is recorded that in the 6th year of the {{ill|Shōwa|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (839) the deity was conferred the rank of Junior Fifth Rank Lower; in the ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}}'' it is recorded that between the 9th and 16th years of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (867–874) the deity was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank Upper to Senior Fifth Rank Lower, and in the 4th year of the {{ill|Genkei|ja|元慶|12=draft}} era (880) to Senior Fourth Rank Upper.A record in the Nagagen period document ''Ueno Province Alternating Records'' lists the rank as Senior First, though no promotion record exists. Later, in the medieval period, the shrine became the Second Shrine of {{ill|Ueno Province|ja|上野国|12=draft}}. However, debate exists as to whether the deity mentioned in these records—with a Ronsha present at another shrine—refers to Miyosawa Akagi Shrine (see {{ill|Akagi Shrine#History|ja|赤城神社#歴史|12=draft}}). In the 14th century collection of legends ''{{ill|Shinto Shu|ja|神道集|12=draft}}'', the small pond of Mount Akagi’s crater lake, the large pond, and the central crater’s Jizodake are deified. The small pond god is associated with {{ill|Kokūzō Bosatsu|ja|虚空蔵菩薩|12=draft}}, the large pond god with {{ill|Senju Kannon|ja|千手観音|12=draft}}, and Jizodake is identified with {{ill|Jizō Bosatsu|ja|地蔵菩薩|12=draft}} (the latter being a later addition). According to records handed down in the West Shrine, the West Shrine enshrined Kokūzō and Senju Kannon, while the East Shrine enshrined Jizō. According to the "Miyagi Murashi", the Miyosawa Akagi Shrine is distinct from the government shrine Akagi seen in texts such as the ''Rokukokushi''. Originally, the East Shrine was established around the late 13th to early 14th century as "Akagi Shrine" along with the flourishing of the Jizodake faith; subsequently, the shrine located in the area known as "Former Miyosawa"The Miyosawa Akagi Shrine tradition states that the shrine grounds were relocated, with the eastern site known as Former Miyosawa. The Utsū Ruins discovered there have been identified as the former shrine site. relocated next to the East Shrine. This new site became the West Shrine, estimated to have been established around the 1st year of the {{ill|Jōwa|ja|貞和|12=draft}} era (circa 1345). The former Miyosawa shrine is also said to have been the mountain shrine of the Nomiya Akagi Shrine. After the West Shrine was relocated, Miyosawa Akagi Shrine came to consist of both an East and a West Shrine, although the longstanding East Shrine was stronger. During the Sengoku period, documents indicate that almost all references to the shrine included "Miyosawa" in the name, not recognizing it as the main shrine of Akagi. However, by the 4th year of the {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|12=draft}} era (1576), after the Nomiya Akagi Shrine in Ninomiya Town was destroyed by local rivals, there were no shrines rivaling the Miyosawa Akagi Shrine and its East Shrine, and it came to be recognized as the main shrine of Akagi.According to the "Miyagi Murashi". ==== Edo Period ==== On February 20 in the 17th year of the {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} era (1612), a donation from residents of Ōmaeda Village (present-day Ōmaeda-cho, Maebashi City) resulted in a row of pine trees being planted along the approach. In the 12th year of the {{ill|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|12=draft}} era (1762), the East Shrine was conferred Senior First Rank, followed by the West Shrine in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiwa|ja|明和|12=draft}} era (1765). In the 12th year of the {{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政|12=draft}} era (1800), the {{ill|Daidō Akagi Shrine|ja|大洞赤城神社|12=draft}} of Maebashi’s Fujimicho, Akagi Mountain, using the title "Main Shrine", initiated litigation against Miyosawa Akagi Shrine’s attendant temple, Jujōji. In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|12=draft}} era (1802), the Miyosawa side appealed to the shogunate’s Temple and Shrine Magistrate, but the matter was resolved by returning it to state jurisdiction. The litigation was prolonged, and an agreement regarding the use of names was reached in the {{ill|Bunka|ja|文久|12=draft}} 13th year (1816). ==== From the Meiji Period Onwards ==== In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft}} era (1869), due to the policy of abolishing Buddhism, two shrine-temples—Ryūseki-ji of the East Shrine and Shinkō-ji of the West Shrine—were closed. Thereafter, the two shrines of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine, formerly East and West, merged into a single shrine. Although documents from the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|12=draft}} era (1802) already treated it as a single shrine, it was officially designated as such in the early Meiji period. However, as the shrine’s records do not mention the merger, the exact timing remains unknown. No buildings were erected at the former West Shrine site, and at the East Shrine site the current shrine buildings (the main hall and the middle gate) were constructed. A record exists of a topping-out ceremony held on November 25 (old calendar) in Meiji 2 (1869). In 1894 (Meiji 27), the worship hall burned down and was later rebuilt. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it was initially a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft}}, later elevated to a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft}}. In 1935 (Shōwa 10), a movement for elevation to a {{ill|Kokuhēisha|ja|国幣社|12=draft}} arose, and in 1944 (Shōwa 19) a provisional decision for {{ill|Kokuhēichūsha|ja|国幣中社|12=draft}} was issued; however, during the process the end of the war and directives from the GHQ led to the abolition of the shrine ranking system, leaving it as a Prefectural Shrine. === Shrine Ranks === * Records in the ''{{ill|Rokukokushi|ja|六国史|12=draft}}'' record the conferral of shrine ranks for "Akagi God" (though interpretations vary beyond this shrine): ** In the 6th year of the {{ill|Shōwa|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (839), in June, he was conferred Junior Fifth Rank Lower (''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft}}'') ** In the 9th year of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承和|12=draft}} era (867), on June 20, he was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank Upper to Senior Fifth Rank Lower (''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft}}'') ** On December 25 of the 11th year of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観|12=draft}} era (869), he was conferred Senior Fifth Rank Upper (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') ** On March 14 of the 16th year of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|貞観|12=draft}} era (874), he was conferred Junior Fourth Rank Lower (''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'') ** On May 25 of the 4th year of the {{ill|Genkei|ja|元慶|12=draft}} era (880), he was conferred Junior Fourth Rank Upper – with the inscription reading either "Akagi Ishi-no-Kami" or "Akagi Numano-Kami"Manuscript variations exist between "Akagi Ishi-no-Kami" and "Akagi Numano-Kami". * After the Rokukokushi period: ** Around the 3rd year of the {{ill|Chōgen|ja|長元|12=draft}} era (circa 1030), he was conferred Senior First Rank (as per the ''Ueno Province Alternating Records'') ** Senior First Rank (as per the ''Ueno Province Shrine Name Records'') – recorded as "Akagi Daimyōjin" * 18th Century: ** In the 12th year of the {{ill|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|12=draft}} era (1762), the East Shrine received Senior First Rank ** In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiwa|ja|明和|12=draft}} era (1765), the West Shrine received Senior First Rank == Shrine Facilities == === Shrine Buildings === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall (Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Property)}}]] The main hall is constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|12=draft}} style with three bays on the front and two on the sides, in a gabled roof design with copper plate roofing. The chigi (roof finials) are internally tapered, with eight support beams (katsugi) installed. It is said, along with the middle gate, to have been built in 1869 (Meiji 2){{Cite web|title=III Akagi Mountain Faith and Historical Scenery of the Southern Foot Settlements|url=https://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/material/files/group/59/rekimachi_2shou_3.pdf|website=Maebashi City|accessdate=2025-02-04}}. Its construction reflects the influences of the then prevalent Shinto-Buddhism separation and restoration of ancient Shinto, and together with the middle gate it is designated as a tangible cultural property of Gunma Prefecture[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01034&insgpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Main Hall and Middle Gate] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). Within the main hall is an inner palace enshrined as the divine seat (kamiza). An inscription behind the door states "Gifted by Minenari Shige Yorin", and it is attributed to the offering by the lord of {{ill|Nintenkimazono Castle|ja|新田金山城|12=draft}}, Minenari Shige Yorin. Constructed in a wooden hōkei style (not “square-style”) with a plank roof and a height of 117 cm, featuring chimaki-adorned pillars and lattice doors reminiscent of Zen style, it is characteristic of the Muromachi period and designated as a tangible cultural property of Gunma Prefecture[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01033&insgpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Inner Palace] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). The middle gate, a four-legged gate standing in front of the main hall, is a gabled roof structure with copper roofing, also said to have been built in 1869 (Meiji 2). The inner palace within the main hall, as well as the main hall and middle gate, were designated as important cultural properties of Gunma Prefecture in 1963 (Showa 38) and 1973 (Showa 48) respectively. File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) haiden.JPG|Worship Hall File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) nakamon.JPG|Middle Gate (Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Property) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) kaguraden.JPG|Kagura Hall === Around the Shrine Buildings === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) tawara-sugi.JPG|thumb|180px|right|{{center|Tawara Cedar (Gunma Prefecture-designated Natural Monument)}}{{small|Middle Gate is at lower left.}}]] The "Tawara Cedar" refers to three large cedar trees standing immediately to the south of the middle gate and its western neighbor. The two trees in front of the main hall stand side by side. According to legend, they were planted as offerings by {{ill|Fujiwara no Hidesato|ja|藤原秀郷|12=draft}} (also known as Tawara Tōta) during his journey to the Ueno government office to subdue {{ill|Taira no Masakado|ja|平将門|12=draft}}. They have been designated as a natural monument by Gunma Prefecture[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01037&insgpos=139.181267133333,36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Tawara Cedar] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). A similar legend is recounted for the cedar at {{ill|Ichinomiya Nukemae Shrine|ja|一之宮貫前神社|12=draft}}, suggesting the aspirations of medieval warriors towards honorOn-site explanatory board.. Many other large cedar trees also stand within the shrine grounds. Also present is the "Jindai Moji Stele", an inscribed stone believed to bear characters from before the introduction of Chinese script, erected in March of Meiji 3 as an artifact of ancient Shinto. The inscription was written by the adopted son of {{ill|Hirata Atsutane|ja|平田鐵胤|12=draft}}, with the divine text composed by his son, En'in. The divine text "Manahitokoronarukowe yoshi" is written in the style of the Abiru script passed down within the Abiru family of Tsushima. Additionally, about 200 m east of the shrine grounds along the road to the Hitsuishi, there is a beech tree designated as a natural monument by the city, and a treasure pagoda (Akagi Tower) designated as a city-important cultural property. File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) shindaimojihi.JPG|Jindai Moji Stele (City-designated Important Cultural Property) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) buna.JPG|Miyosawa Beech (City-designated Natural Monument) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) keidaisandou.JPG|Approach Path in the Shrine Grounds File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) ike.JPG|Sacred Pond === Within Mount Akagi === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) hituishi.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Hitsuishi (Gunma Prefecture-designated Historic Site)}}]] A ritual site centered on a massive stone known as "Hitsuishi" is located about 1.3 km up Mount Akagi from the shrine grounds ({{Coord|36|29|38.43|N|139|10|30.42|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=Hitsuishi}}). It measures approximately 4.7 m in length, 2.7 m in width, 2.8 m in height, with a circumference of 12.2 m. Numerous ritual objects have been found in the vicinity, and it was designated as a historic site by Gunma Prefecture in 1963 (Showa 38)[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.178167933333,36.4909051337386&gscl=16000&ssiz=500,500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000100&id=01036&insgpos=139.178167933333,36.4909051337386&accept=939820130608102329 Hitsuishi] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System).[http://www.gunmaibun.org/cgi-bin/iseki/database.cgi?cmd=dp&num=23369&dp= Hitsuishi] (Gunma Prefecture Buried Cultural Property Survey Group). === Approach (Sandō) === [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) soumon.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Soumon (Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Property)}}]] The approach from the Soumon to National Route 353 is lined with numerous pine trees, preserved as an Edo-period pine avenue. According to the "Akagi Shrine Chronicle", in the 17th year of the {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft}} era (1612) approximately 1,200 pine trees were planted along the approach by donation from Hikobe of Ōmaeda Village (present-day Ōmaeda-cho, Maebashi City), each estimated to be around 400 years old. In addition, about 30,000 rhododendron plants were also planted, making the area famous in spring[http://akagi-yama.jp/archives/330 Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Pine Avenue and Rhododendron Group] (Akagi Mountain Portal Site). The Soumon is a Takamado-mon built during the Edo period (exact date unknown). It is located about 450 m south of the shrine grounds ({{Coord|36|28|49.61|N|139|10|39.36|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=Soumon}}). Although the "Akagi Shrine Chronicle" records its construction in the 1st year of the {{ill|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|12=draft}} era (1751), some older materials are also evident. As few Takamado-mon from the early modern period exist in Gunma Prefecture, it was designated as a tangible cultural property in 1978 (Showa 53)[http://www2.wagamachi-guide.com/gunma/map.asp?gpos=139.181267133333%2C36.4813478449848&gscl=16000&ssiz=500%2C500&sid=5026&galay=0000000000000010&insgpos=139.181267133333%2C36.4813478449848&accept=939820130608102329&Map.x=246&Map.y=352 Akagi Shrine Soumon] (Gunma Prefecture Cultural Property Information System). File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) ishidono.JPG|Ishidono (City-designated Important Cultural Property) File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) sandou.JPG|Approach Path File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) ichinotorii.JPG|First Torii ({{Coord|36|28|36.74|N|139|10|43.16|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=First Torii}}) == Festivals == * Shihō Haijinja and New Year Festival ({{ill|January 1|ja|1月1日|12=draft}})The festival events are recorded in the shrine’s tradition. * Shūsei-e ({{ill|January 5|ja|1月5日|12=draft}}) * Tsutsugayu Sacred Event ({{ill|January 15|ja|1月15日|12=draft}}) * Nenki Festival ({{ill|February 19|ja|2月19日|12=draft}}) * Gochin Festival (afternoon in March) * Sacred Procession (early April) – A mikoshi parade from Nomiya Akagi Shrine to Miyosawa. * Annual Festival ({{ill|May 5|ja|5月5日|12=draft}}) * Gochin Festival (afternoon in November) * Sacred Procession (early December) – A mikoshi parade from Nomiya Akagi Shrine to Miyosawa. * New Rice Thanksgiving Festival (Shinjō-sai) ({{ill|December 10|ja|12月10日|12=draft}}) == Cultural Properties == === Important Artifacts (National Designation) === * Jadeite magatama (excavated near the Akagi Shrine Hitsuishi) – Designated on July 13, 1939 (Showa 14)'Catalog of Important Artifacts' (Shibunkaku, 1972), Volume 1, p.30The Maebashi City official website gives the designation date as "July 30, Showa 14", but the official gazette date is July 13 of the same year. === Gunma Prefecture-designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Inner Palace of the Main Hall – Designated on September 4, 1963 (Showa 38). ** Main Hall and Middle Gate – Designated on April 25, 1973 (Showa 48). ** Ancient Documents – 45 documents from Eiroku 3 (1560) to Keichō 18 (1613). Designated on April 25, Showa 48. ** Soumon – Designated on August 25, Showa 53. * Historic Sites ** Hitsuishi – Designated on September 4, 1963 (Showa 38), with an additional designation on June 25, 1985 (Showa 60). * Natural Monuments ** The Tawara Cedar of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine – Designated on April 25, 1973 (Showa 48). === Maebashi City-designated Cultural Properties === * Important Cultural Properties (Tangible) ** Jindai Moji Stele in the shrine grounds – Designated on April 1, 1978 (Showa 53). ** Treasure Pagoda (Akagi Tower) – Designated on April 1, 1978 (Showa 53). * Important Intangible Folk Cultural Properties ** Miyosawa Akagi Shrine Taida Kagura – 13 troupes are offered on January 1, January 5, and May 5. Designated on July 4, Showa 60. * Natural Monuments ** The Beech of Miyosawa – Designated on April 1, 1980 (Showa 55). == Related Locations == * Former Miyosawa (Murozawa, Kasukawa-cho, Maebashi City) : Considered to be the old shrine site of the West Shrine prior to its relocation. Foundation stones, presumed to date from the Heian period, have been discovered'Place Names of Gunma Prefecture' – Murozawa Section, Kasukawa Village, Setagaya District. * Utsū Ruins ({{ill|Utsū Ruins|ja|宇通遺跡|12=draft}}) (Nakanosawa, Kasukawa-cho, Maebashi City, {{ウィキ座標|36|29|20.11|N|139|12|02.23|E|region:JP-10_type:landmark|name=Utsū Ruins}}) : Ruins located in a forest in the upper reaches of the Kasukawa River. Discovered during a forest fire in 1965 (Showa 40), investigations were partial but identified foundation stone structures suggesting the remains of a temple from the syncretic period. It is speculated to be the former location of Akagi Shrine, and its relation to the multi-storied pagoda on the mountain (in {{ill|Kiryū City|ja|桐生市|12=draft}}, built in the 20th year of {{ill|Enryaku|ja|延暦|12=draft}} (801)) has been noted'Place Names of Gunma Prefecture' – Utsū Ruins Section, Kasukawa Village, Setagaya District.[http://www.gunmaibun.org/cgi-bin/iseki/database.cgi?cmd=dp&num=22585&dp= Utsū Ruins] (Gunma Prefecture Buried Cultural Property Survey Group). == Local Information == '''Location''' * {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft}}{{ill|Maebashi City|ja|前橋市|12=draft}} Miyosawa-cho, 114 '''Access''' * From {{ill|Jōmō Electric Railway|ja|上毛電気鉄道|12=draft}}{{ill|Jōmō Line|ja|上毛電気鉄道上毛線|12=draft}} {{ill|Ōogoe Station|ja|大胡駅|12=draft}}, take the [http://www.city.maebashi.gunma.jp/kurashi/143/168/166/p001744.html {{ill|Maebashi City Furusato Bus|ja|前橋市ふるさとバス|12=draft}}] (demand bus) and alight at the "Akagi Shrine" bus stop (a short walk from there). '''Surroundings''' * {{ill|Akagi South-Facing Senbonzakura|ja|赤城南面千本桜|12=draft}} – A cherry tree avenue extending approximately 3.5 km. == References == '''Notes''' {{Reflist|group="note"}} '''Sources''' {{Reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * "Akagi Shrine Yuiosho-ryakuki" (Shrine Tradition Record) * Miyagi Murashi Editorial Committee, ed. "Miyagi Murashi" (Miyagi Village, 1973) * "Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei: Place Names of Gunma Prefecture" (Heibonsha) – Section on Akagi Shrine in Setagaya District, Miyagi Village * Kajima Katsuo, "Akagi Shrine" in {{ill|Kenichi Tanikawa|ja|谷川健一|12=draft}} ed., ''Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Sites – 11 Kanto'' (Hakusuisha) == See Also == {{Commonscat|Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa)|赤城神社}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|12=draft}} ** {{ill|Akagi Shrine (Maebashi City Fujimicho, Mount Akagi)|ja|赤城神社 (前橋市富士見町赤城山)|12=draft}} ** {{ill|Nomiya Akagi Shrine|ja|二宮赤城神社|12=draft}} == External Links == * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/250201.html {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|12=draft}}] – Kokugakuin University 21st Century COE Program “Compilation of Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials” {{神道 横}} {{citation needed|あかきしんしやまえはししみよさわまち}} {{draft categories| [[Category:History of Maebashi City]] [[Category:Architecture of Maebashi City]] [[Category:Meishin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinaisha of Ueno Province]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrines in Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Akagi Shrines]] [[Category:11]] [[Category:Completion tier 2]] [[Category:New]] }} [[ja:赤城神社 (前橋市三夜沢町)]] [[sn:Miyosawa Akagi Shrine]] [[ja:赤城神社]]

'''Akagi Shrine''' (赤城神社) is a {{ill|Shinto|ja|神道|12=draft|12=draft}} shrine located in {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft|12=draft}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=draft|12=draft}}) and is also regarded as a potential site of the Second Shrine of {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国|12=draft|12=draft}}. It was formerly designated as a Prefectural Shrine under the pre-World War II Modern Shrine Ranking System. It is officially called "Akagi Shrine," but to distinguish it from other shrines of the same name, it is also referred to as "'''Miyosawa Akagi Shrine'''" (三夜沢赤城神社). Among the approximately 300 Akagi shrines across the country, especially centered around the Kantō region, this shrine is considered one of the most likely to be the original main shrine. == Overview == The shrine sits on the southern mountainside of {{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft|12=draft}} in central Gunma Prefecture. Prior to the Meiji period, the shrine consisted of two separate shrines (East and West), but they were unified into a single entity during the Meiji era. The approach to the shrine diverges into three directions at the first torii gate: toward {{ill|Ōgo|ja|大胡町|12=draft|12=draft}} in the south, Naegashima in the east, and Ichinoseki in the west. The path toward Ōgo retains a row of pine trees planted during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft|12=draft}}. The honden (main sanctuary) and nakamon (middle gate) are designated as Important Cultural Properties by Gunma Prefecture. Approximately 500 meters south of the honden along the path is the sōmon (main gate), which is also a prefectural cultural property. Between the haiden (worship hall) and nakamon stands the "Tawara Sugi," a cedar tree designated as a Natural Monument by the prefecture. Additionally, the grounds include the "Monument of Jindai Moji," established in March 1870, a relic of {{ill|Fukko Shintō|ja|復古神道|12=draft|12=draft}}, and designated as an Important Cultural Property by Maebashi City. == Worshipped deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}}}} * Akagi-no-Kami * {{ill|Toyoki-Irihiko-no-Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft|12=draft}} == History == === Establishment === The shrine's establishment date is unknown. According to shrine tradition, it was founded when Toyoki-Irihiko-no-Mikoto began ruling over {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上毛野国|12=draft|12=draft}}, accompanied by Ōkuninushi. About 1.3 km up from the shrine lies a ritual site centered around a large rock known as {{ill|Hitsuishi|ja|櫃石|12=draft|12=draft}}, which indicates the presence of ancient Shinto practices. === General History ===
Transition of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine
{{familytree/start|style=font-size:90%}} ... (family tree preserved as in source) {{familytree/end}}
=== Heian Period === According to the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft|12=draft}}, in 839 (Jōwa 6), the shrine received the rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade. The {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft|12=draft}} records that the shrine was promoted multiple times between 867 (Jōgan 9) and 880 (Gangyō 4), eventually reaching Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade. It is said that by around 1028 (Chōgen 9), it was promoted to Senior First Rank. {{Shrine | name = Akagi Shrine | religious_affiliation = {{ill|Shinto|ja|神道|12=draft|12=draft}} | image = {{ill|Akagi Shrine (Miyosawa) Front View|ja|赤城神社 (Miyosawa) shoumen|12=draft|12=draft}}

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=draft|12=draft}} ({{ill|Meishin Taisha|ja|名神大社|12=draft|12=draft}}) {{ill|Ronsha|ja|論社|12=draft|12=draft}}, as well as a Nomiya Ronsha of {{ill|Ueno Province|ja|上野国|12=draft|12=draft}}, and formerly a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although its official name is "Akagi Shrine", to distinguish it from other Akagi Shrines it is also called "'''Miyosawa Akagi Shrine''' (みよさわあかぎじんじゃ)". It is one of the principal shrines, presumed to be the main shrine among approximately 300 Akagi Shrines across the country, mainly in the {{ill|Kanto region|ja|関東地方|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Overview == Located on the southern hillside of {{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft|12=draft}} in central {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県|12=draft|12=draft}}, the shrine was once regarded as having two shrines (East and West) before the Meiji era, but later became a single shrine. The approach splits into three directions: one with the first torii leading south toward the {{ill|Grand Torii|ja|大鳥居|12=draft|12=draft}} and the Ōogomachi area, one east toward Naegashima, and one west toward Ichinoseki. The road continuing in the Ōogomachi direction still retains a pine avenue planted during the Edo period. Both the main hall and the middle gate are designated as important cultural properties by the prefecture. Along the approach, about 500 meters south of the main hall, stands the Soumon (main gate), also designated as an important cultural property. Additionally, between the worship hall and the middle gate, immediately in front of the middle gate, is the "Tawara Cedar", a natural monument designated by Gunma Prefecture. The shrine grounds also include a "Jindai Moji Stele" erected in March 1870 (Meiji 3), regarded as an artifact of the restoration of ancient Shinto, and designated as an important cultural property by the city. == Worshipped Deities (Saijin) == {{see also|{{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|12=draft|12=draft}}}} * {{ill|Akagi God|ja|赤城神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Akagi no Kami) * {{ill|Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft|12=draft}} (Ōkuninushi-no-mikoto) == History == [[File:MountAkagi.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|{{ill|Mount Akagi|ja|赤城山|12=draft|12=draft}} (Sacred Object)}}]] === Establishment === The establishment date is unknown. According to the shrine’s tradition, in ancient times when {{ill|Toyoki Irihiko-no-mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|12=draft|12=draft}} came to rule {{ill|Kozuke Province|ja|上毛野国|12=draft|12=draft}}, he enshrined {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|12=draft|12=draft}}. About 1.3 km uphill from the shrine, a ritual site centered on a stone called the "Hitsuishi" remains, suggesting ancient worship practices. === Chronological Overview ===

==== Heian Period ==== In the ''{{ill|Zoku Nihon Kōki|ja|続日本後紀|12=draft|12=draft}}'', it is recorded that in the 6th year of the {{ill|Shōwa|ja|承和|12=draft|12=draft}} era (839) the deity was conferred the rank of Junior Fifth Rank Lower; in the ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|12=draft|12=draft}}'' it is recorded that between the 9th and 16th years of the {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承和|12=draft|12=draft}} era (867–874) the deity was promoted from Junior Fifth Rank Upper to Senior Fifth Rank Lower, and in the 4th year of the {{ill|Genkei|ja|元慶|12=draft|12=draft}} era (880) to Senior Fourth Rank Upper.A record in the Nagagen period document ''Ueno Province Alternating Records'' lists the rank as Senior First, though no promotion record exists. Later, in the medieval period, the shrine became the Second Shrine of {{ill|Ueno Province|ja|上野国|12=draft|12=draft}}. However, debate exists as to whether the deity mentioned in these records—with a Ronsha present at another shrine—refers to Miyosawa Akagi Shrine (see {{ill|Akagi Shrine#History|ja|赤城神社#歴史|12=draft|12=draft}}). In the 14th century collection of legends ''{{ill|Shinto Shu|ja|神道集|12=draft|12=draft}}'', the small pond of Mount Akagi’s crater lake, the large pond, and the central crater’s Jizodake are deified. The small pond god is associated with {{ill|Kokūzō Bosatsu|ja|虚空蔵菩薩|12=draft|12=draft}}, the large pond god with {{ill|Senju Kannon|ja|千手観音|12=draft|12=draft}}, and Jizodake is identified with {{ill|Jizō Bosatsu|ja|地蔵菩薩|12=draft|12=draft}} (the latter being a later addition). According to records handed down in the West Shrine, the West Shrine enshrined Kokūzō and Senju Kannon, while the East Shrine enshrined Jizō. According to the "Miyagi Murashi", the Miyosawa Akagi Shrine is distinct from the government shrine Akagi seen in texts such as the ''Rokukokushi''. Originally, the East Shrine was established around the late 13th to early 14th century as "Akagi Shrine" along with the flourishing of the Jizodake faith; subsequently, the shrine located in the area known as "Former Miyosawa"The Miyosawa Akagi Shrine tradition states that the shrine grounds were relocated, with the eastern site known as Former Miyosawa. The Utsū Ruins discovered there have been identified as the former shrine site. relocated next to the East Shrine. This new site became the West Shrine, estimated to have been established around the 1st year of the {{ill|Jōwa|ja|貞和|12=draft|12=draft}} era (circa 1345). The former Miyosawa shrine is also said to have been the mountain shrine of the Nomiya Akagi Shrine. After the West Shrine was relocated, Miyosawa Akagi Shrine came to consist of both an East and a West Shrine, although the longstanding East Shrine was stronger. During the Sengoku period, documents indicate that almost all references to the shrine included "Miyosawa" in the name, not recognizing it as the main shrine of Akagi. However, by the 4th year of the {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1576), after the Nomiya Akagi Shrine in Ninomiya Town was destroyed by local rivals, there were no shrines rivaling the Miyosawa Akagi Shrine and its East Shrine, and it came to be recognized as the main shrine of Akagi.According to the "Miyagi Murashi". ==== Edo Period ==== On February 20 in the 17th year of the {{ill|Keichō|ja|慶長|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1612), a donation from residents of Ōmaeda Village (present-day Ōmaeda-cho, Maebashi City) resulted in a row of pine trees being planted along the approach. In the 12th year of the {{ill|Hōreki|ja|宝暦|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1762), the East Shrine was conferred Senior First Rank, followed by the West Shrine in the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiwa|ja|明和|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1765). In the 12th year of the {{ill|Kansei|ja|寛政|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1800), the {{ill|Daidō Akagi Shrine|ja|大洞赤城神社|12=draft|12=draft}} of Maebashi’s Fujimicho, Akagi Mountain, using the title "Main Shrine", initiated litigation against Miyosawa Akagi Shrine’s attendant temple, Jujōji. In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1802), the Miyosawa side appealed to the shogunate’s Temple and Shrine Magistrate, but the matter was resolved by returning it to state jurisdiction. The litigation was prolonged, and an agreement regarding the use of names was reached in the {{ill|Bunka|ja|文久|12=draft|12=draft}} 13th year (1816). ==== From the Meiji Period Onwards ==== In the 2nd year of the {{ill|Meiji|ja|明治|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1869), due to the policy of abolishing Buddhism, two shrine-temples—Ryūseki-ji of the East Shrine and Shinkō-ji of the West Shrine—were closed. Thereafter, the two shrines of Miyosawa Akagi Shrine, formerly East and West, merged into a single shrine. Although documents from the 2nd year of the {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|12=draft|12=draft}} era (1802) already treated it as a single shrine, it was officially designated as such in the early Meiji period. However, as the shrine’s records do not mention the merger, the exact timing remains unknown. No buildings were erected at the former West Shrine site, and at the East Shrine site the current shrine buildings (the main hall and the middle gate) were constructed. A record exists of a topping-out ceremony held on November 25 (old calendar) in Meiji 2 (1869). In 1894 (Meiji 27), the worship hall burned down and was later rebuilt. Under the modern shrine ranking system, it was initially a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|12=draft|12=draft}}, later elevated to a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|12=draft|12=draft}}. In 1935 (Shōwa 10), a movement for elevation to a {{ill|Kokuhēisha|ja|国幣社|12=draft|12=draft}} arose, and in 1944 (Shōwa 19) a provisional decision for {{ill|Kokuhēichūsha|ja|国幣中社|12=draft|12=draft}} was issued; however, during the process the end of the war and directives from the GHQ led to the abolition of the shrine ranking system, leaving it as a Prefectural Shrine. === Shrine Ranks === *
